martello.introLede: Martello is built around synthesized drum voices with a strong resonator and modal-synthesis influence.
martello.introBody: Its sound is shaped by the idea of struck objects, vibrating bodies, wood, metal, membranes, and physical percussion behavior. Martello and MartelloX2 are focused drum synthesizers, not sample players. Design kicks, snares, hats, and percussion with immediate control, per-voice model selection, and optional dual-engine routing for full-kit patterns in one plugin.
martello.statement: Martello is not a sample pack. It is a synthesized drum instrument with resonator and modal character: dry, direct, and physical.
martello.modulatorAlt: Martello Dark Modulator Voice 1 interface screenshot
martello.modelTitle: Every voice chooses its own physics.
martello.modelBody: Classic, Classic Extended, Classic Hats, Digital, Analog, Digital+, Toms, Clap, Wood, Ride, Cymbal, Cowbell, Low Bongo, Mid Bongo, High Bongo, Glass Clave, Tambourine, Maracas, Open Percussion Extension, Charlie, Metallic, Robots, Robots Expert, and the available Expert variants. Switch modes and the control panel instantly reconfigures to expose the parameters of the selected engine.
martello.producersStatement: Made for producers who want drums that feel played, tuned, pushed, and shaped. Not just selected from a folder.

martello.validationP1: Every MontroneDSP release is checked through automated validation, internal signal analysis, stress testing, and human musical testing.
martello.validationP2: Validation includes pluginval correctness level 10, sample-rate testing up to 192 kHz, automation stress tests, repeated load/unload checks, multi-instance sessions, save/reload verification, preset recall, MIDI triggering, rapid parameter changes, offline rendering, and internal monitoring for signal integrity.
martello.validationP3: MartelloX2 is additionally tested for dual-engine behavior, multi-output routing, heavier session conditions, and real-world usability inside actual DAW projects.
martello.feedback1Quote: The FM sounds with modulation are really handy. My impression so far is that this is a very well-priced device with good customer support.
martello.feedback1Meta: UK · Sungate Records · Art Bei Ton
martello.devP1: Martello is an idea that started forming around 2014, when I was exploring Eurorack synthesis, resonators, and modal synthesis. I was always drawn to those tones because they felt more physical, natural, and alive than many traditional electronic drum sounds. They had the feeling of objects being struck, vibrating, and reacting in a real space.
martello.devP2: For a long time, I tried to reach that feeling with samples, but it never really worked for me.
martello.devP3: Over time, the idea started moving more clearly toward synthesized drums, using resonators and physical approaches rather than relying only on samples.
martello.devP4: That direction became the foundation of Martello: a focused drum instrument made to feel immediate, responsive, and alive. While I was also working on a much more complex instrument, Martello naturally became something more direct, simple to understand, quick to use, and centered on sound.
martello.devP5: The interface follows the same idea: no complicated submenus, with the main controls visible and ready to shape. Martello is built around limitations, but in a creative way, giving artists a starting point to design their own drum kits and then place them inside their own effects, space, and workflow.
martello.noSeqP1: We deliberately chose not to build a sequencer into Martello. Adding one would have changed the nature of the instrument, shifting attention away from its synthesis panels and toward an internal workflow that could never suit every artist. Martello is meant to remain open: a sound-design instrument that responds naturally to the sequencer, controller, generative system, or performance method you already prefer.
martello.noSeqTip1Title: Tip 1: For Ableton Live users, Martello and Martello X2 pair especially well with Instant Haus by Alexkid.
martello.instantHausAlt: Instant Haus Max for Live device by Alexkid
martello.noSeqP2: This Max for Live device can quickly generate musical drum patterns while still offering detailed control over individual parts, velocity, swing, timing shifts, variation, and randomization. Instead of locking Martello inside a fixed sequencer, this combination lets one device concentrate on rhythm and movement while Martello remains focused entirely on synthesis and sound. Instant Haus is now officially discontinued, but it remains an excellent companion for users who already have access to it.
martello.noSeqP3: Load Martello after Instant Haus, route its generated MIDI notes to the appropriate voices, and an initial groove can emerge almost immediately. From there, every sound can be reshaped directly from Martello’s front panel, turning the generated rhythm into a personal drum kit rather than a finished preset. This reflects the broader idea behind the instrument: provide a strong and immediate starting point, then leave enough space for the artist to transform it.
martello.noSeqTip2P1: Load Martello X2 and select the same drum model for Voice 1 and Voice 4. Digital, Analog, and the Legacy synthesis models are especially effective for this technique. Then reduce the Punch control on Voice 4 to nearly zero. Voice 1 can remain the main kick, while Voice 4 becomes a sustained bass layer derived from the same synthesis model.
martello.noSeqTip2P2: Because both sounds come from closely related sources, the kick and bass naturally share the same tonal character. They can be tuned perfectly together for a tight, unified low end, or deliberately separated to create more tension and movement.
martello.noSeqTip2P3: With traditional drum machines, achieving this degree of control often required circuit modifications, resampling, or additional processing. In Martello X2, the same idea is immediate: one voice provides the impact, while the other transforms the underlying drum synthesis into bass.
martello.noSeqTip2P4: This technique is the conceptual foundation of the Jak2 preset, inspired by a nearly forgotten Naughty Dog masterpiece. Load the preset, hear the kick-and-bass relationship in action, then adjust the tuning, decay, and balance to make the room as bass-heavy as you like.
martello.noSeqTip3P1: We strongly recommend using Martello X2 in multi-output mode. Routing each voice to its own channel gives you much better control over gain staging, balance, automation, and processing, while opening the instrument up to a far more creative multitrack workflow.
martello.noSeqTip3P2: In minimal, abstract, and experimental forms of house and techno, a single percussion sound can become much more than part of the rhythm. It can become the lead instrument, the main hook, or even the defining element of the entire track. With separate outputs, each Martello voice can be treated deliberately with your favourite reverbs, delays, distortion, modulation, or more complex effect chains, allowing the instrument to sit at the centre of the production rather than simply behind it.
martello.noSeqTip3P3: We deliberately chose not to include built-in effects in Martello. We did not want to turn it into another generic all-in-one instrument filled with interchangeable processing. Instead, Martello focuses on synthesis and leaves space for you to shape its sounds using your own effects, your own spaces, and your own signal chains. This allows the instrument to enter your sonic world rather than forcing you into ours.
martello.noSeqTip4P1: If your studio includes an analog mixer or other outboard equipment, we strongly recommend routing Martello X2’s individual outputs from your DAW into separate hardware channels. This gives you immediate hands-on control over every voice, while adding the sonic colour, saturation, and natural response of your analog signal path.
martello.noSeqTip4P2: Working this way also makes it possible to manipulate the sounds quickly with hardware EQ, compression, distortion, sends, and external effects. Small movements on the mixer can radically transform the rhythm, opening up an almost endless range of combinations and encouraging a more physical and spontaneous approach to sound design.
martello.noSeqTip4P3: The result is something close to an expandable modular drum machine, but with the affordability and convenience of a multi-instance software instrument. You retain preset storage, complete project recall, automation, and the ability to reopen a session exactly as you left it, while gaining the tactile control and character of an analog studio workflow.
martello.noSeqTip4P4: Martello provides the synthesis engine; the mixer and outboard chain become an extension of the instrument.

aurashimmer.ownershipTitle: VST3 on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
aurashimmer.ownershipBody1: Aura ships as 64-bit VST3 only - no standalone application. macOS includes a .pkg installer, or copy the MontroneDSP VST3 folder into your system or user plugin directory. On Windows, place it in your VST3 folder (typically C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3). On Linux, use your system or user VST3 directory, then rescan in your DAW.
aurashimmer.ownershipBody2: After checkout, your license key appears on the Aura download page. Open Aura, paste the key in License or About, and activate. Each perpetual license covers up to three machines.

membrana.lead: Early access ships two of five synthesis engines  -  Marimba and Modern Modal  -  united by exciter physics and resonator geometry.
membrana.introLede: Early access on 10 September ships two of five planned engines for membranes, bodies, and tuned percussion  -  built around exciter physics and resonator geometry.
membrana.introBody: Membrana is a multimodal synthesizer, not a sample player. Marimba brings classic membrane strike and bar resonance. Modern Modal shapes resonant body tone. Three more engines follow in later releases.
membrana.statement: One instrument, five engines planned  -  early access starts with Marimba and Modern Modal.
membrana.marimbaBody: Struck membrane and marimba bar synthesis  -  skin tension, body knock, and the raw attack of physical instruments distilled into playable sound. Shape contour, damping, and decay for drums, skins, bars, and tuned percussion.
membrana.modalTitle: Shape the modes. Tune the body.
membrana.modalBody: Modal resonator modeling for membranes, plates, and vibrating bodies. Sculpt overtone structure, geometry, and damping with surgical control  -  from dry, focused strike to evolving harmonic bloom and long, singing decay.
membrana.audioLede: Nobuo Uematsu  -  <cite>To Zanarkand</cite> arranged with two Membrana voices and Galleria spatial FX  -  marimba strike, modal body tone, and sculpted hall space in one piece.
membrana.audioIframeTitle: Nobuo Uematsu  -  To Zanarkand: two Membrana voices with Galleria FX

galleria.lead: Spectral gallery reverb with bright public-space reflections and immersive spatial motion.
galleria.introLede: Immersive spatial processing built around bright hall reflections, hybrid delay, and motion-driven 3D placement.
galleria.introBody: Galleria is a spectral gallery reverb  -  not a static room preset. Shape space, delay, orbit, and texture in one focused panel, from dry public architecture to long tails that move through the field.
galleria.statement: Galleria is a spatial instrument where reflections, delay, and motion are composed together  -  bright, smooth, and deliberately placed.
galleria.spaceBody: Classic and spatial reverb modes with independent early/late balance, density, and diffusion. Filter the space, freeze the tail, and push reflections into motion without losing clarity.
galleria.motionTitle: Place the source. Move the field.
galleria.motionBody: Source X/Y/Z placement, orbit rate and depth, width, doppler, occlusion, and air  -  with a live spatial radar for performance-led positioning. Delay and space follow the same motion logic for cohesive immersion.

swara.punchline: In Sanskrit, svara means voice. Give yours a new one.
swara.offerNote: Official Linux VST3 is available here. Get official builds from the store.
swara.linuxLicenseAccept: I have read and accept the GNU General Public License v3 for Swara XT Linux before downloading. You can also read the official GPL text at gnu.org.
swara.machinesBody: SWARA XT can be CPU intensive with complex patches or multiple instances. Filter Quality modes (since 1.1.0) add High, Normal, and Eco from the right-click menu so you can trade CPU for the same filter character when needed. Minimum is a modern 64-bit VST3 host, 8 GB RAM, 200 MB disk, and Intel Core i7 / AMD Ryzen 5 or equivalent. On Mac, Intel Core i7 or Apple Silicon with comparable multicore performance. On Linux, x86_64.
swara.releaseIntro: SWARA XT 1.2.0 is now available. This release brings an integrated sequencer, so repeating melodic and modulation patterns live inside the instrument.
swara.releaseLibrary: Use it for bass lines, performance loops, filter-driven phrases, and more experimental sequences, with the same direct, hardware-like feel as the rest of the panel.
swara.releaseNextBody: A second filter personality and onboard effects are planned for future updates, without compromising SWARA XT's hardware-like, direct character.
swara.introTitle: A large monosynth with hardware-like sound.
swara.introLede: Deep modulation and an immediate hands-on architecture.
swara.introBody: SWARA XT is a full-scale monophonic synthesizer built around a powerful engine, a characterful filter, extensive modulation, and a direct hardware-inspired layout. Oscillators, filter, envelopes, animation, and sequencing sit in one instrument that can move from precise to saturated and highly animated. Bass lines have weight, resonant sequences stay physical, leads can get sharp and expressive, and sustained sounds keep movement.
swara.statement: स्वर  -  tone as an instrument. Hybrid monosynth design with immediate, musical response.
swara.audioIframeTitle: SWARA XT - Hybrid Monosynth SoundCloud playlist
swara.openShotAlt: Swara XT Jungle skin full interface
swara.coloursBody: Pastel, Neon Cobalt, Jungle, Rosso Corsa, and Midnight Gold. Each skin changes the look of the panel and keeps the same layout and workflow. Browse and save presets from the main panel, including user presets.
swara.decorationAlt: Swara XT Pastel skin with PCB-trace decoration dividers
swara.usesTitle: Electronic music, sequencing, and detailed sound design.
swara.usesBody: Heavy basses, resonant sequences, aggressive mono leads, acid-style lines, synthetic percussion, sharp plucks, drones, metallic tones, evolving sequences, and hardware-style mono patches. Also at home in techno, electro, industrial, IDM, ambient, drone, and bass music.
swara.oscTitle: Two sources, shaped before the filter.
swara.oscBody: Each main oscillator has independent model, pitch, and waveform variation, so the raw sound is already decided before mixer and filter. Clean fundamentals, dense harmonics, sharper digital structures, unstable tones, octave layering, and strongly animated waveforms. The mixer is part of the sound: balance changes how the filter responds, can reinforce the fundamental, or thicken the source.
swara.filterBody: Move from rounded low-frequency weight to sharp resonant tones and strongly articulated sequences. Envelope and modulation let the filter ride with the patch: heavy filtered bass, self-emphasised harmonics, envelope sweeps, rhythmic filtering, and slowly evolving tonal movement.
swara.motionTitle: Envelopes, LFOs, and a readable panel.
swara.motionBody: Two envelopes shape amplitude, filtering, and modulation, from tight physical attacks to longer unfolding. Two LFOs cover vibrato, filter movement, waveform animation, slow drift, and more obvious cyclic behaviour. Dedicated visualisers keep envelope and LFO shapes readable while you program.
swara.matrixTitle: Routes and patterns on the instrument.
swara.matrixBody: The modulation matrix connects sources to destinations without leaving the main panel, so a patch can develop internally. The integrated sequencer adds repeating melodic and modulation patterns, from bass lines and performance loops to filter-driven phrases and more experimental sequences.
swara.formatBody: The official Linux package includes the VST3 plugin and a standalone application. Other official builds are on the store. Copy Swara XT.vst3 into your VST3 folder and rescan in the DAW. On Windows a typical location is C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3. On Linux, use your system or user VST3 directory.
swara.linuxTitle: Built for Linux and open-source software.
swara.linuxLead1: At MontroneDSP, we are strong believers in Linux and open-source software.
swara.linuxLead2: Linux has become an increasingly capable platform for music production, offering excellent performance, flexibility, and a growing ecosystem of professional audio tools. We actively support Linux and test our plugins on a selection of commonly used distributions and desktop environments.
swara.linuxTestedIntro: Our Linux builds are tested on:
swara.linuxUbuntuBody: A stable and widely supported choice for audio production. Ubuntu LTS is our primary reference environment and is a good option for users who want a conventional Linux desktop with long-term support.
swara.linuxSteamBody1: A stable, polished option for users who prefer a preconfigured KDE-based environment. Best suited to Flatpak-based DAWs such as Bitwig and user-installed plug-ins. Because SteamOS uses an immutable system image, advanced system-level audio modifications may require additional setup.
swara.linuxSteamCaution: Caution: the SteamOS installer can wipe existing disk data. Follow the correct install procedure carefully, and always back up important files first.
swara.linuxRecBody1: If you are new to Linux and want the most straightforward, conventional setup for music production, Ubuntu LTS remains an excellent starting point.
swara.linuxRecBody2: For a preconfigured KDE desktop and Flatpak-based DAWs, SteamOS is a tested alternative — with the caveats noted above, including the installer disk-wipe risk.
swara.linuxRecBody3: Linux audio setups can vary considerably between distributions, audio servers, DAWs, drivers, and system configurations. For this reason, we recommend keeping your system updated and using the current version of your DAW and plugin host whenever possible.
swara.linuxFormatsBody1: Our Linux plugins are distributed in VST3 format.
swara.linuxFormatsBody2: When installing manually, make sure your DAW is configured to scan the directory containing the plugin. After installation, restarting or rescanning your DAW may be required before the plugin appears.
swara.linuxOpenBody1: Open source is an important part of the MontroneDSP philosophy.
swara.linuxOpenBody2: Where possible, we contribute to and build upon open technologies, and several of our projects are made available publicly so that musicians, developers, and curious users can explore, learn from, modify, and contribute to the software.
swara.shruthiCredit: Parts of the synthesis engine are derived from the Mutable Instruments Shruthi-1 firmware by Émilie Gillet.
swara.linuxOpenBody3: We believe Linux and open-source development can play an important role in keeping music technology accessible, transparent, and open to experimentation.

laya.punchline: In Sanskrit, laya means rhythm. An ever-growing collection of old and new drum-sequencing algorithms in one digital drum machine.
laya.offerNote: All Laya builds will be free.
laya.introTitle: Rhythms that evolve, mutate, and stay playable.
laya.introLede: Lo-fi drums and a performance sequencer built for ideas that move. All Laya builds will be free.
laya.introBody: Laya brings together a curated collection of selected, experimental and previously unreleased drum-sequencing algorithms in a single instrument. Its sequencing engines range from focused techno and drum & bass generators to more exploratory rhythmic systems, with an emphasis on patterns that feel playable, mutable and alive rather than simply random.
laya.releaseMacTitle: Two ways to work, one instrument.
laya.releaseMacBody: Laya can be operated through a traditional GUI, a fast command-line interface, or both at the same time. Generate, mutate, lock, randomize and reshape rhythms in real time, then use its internal drum voices or send the resulting MIDI directly to external instruments and drum racks.
laya.releaseNextBody: At its core, Laya is a powerful performance sequencer: deterministic when needed, unpredictable when invited, and designed to move continuously between repetition and variation.
laya.joinLede: Have your own idea for a sequencer?
laya.joinBody1: We’re open to integrating new rule-based generative sequencers into Laya. If you have an original sequencing concept, algorithm, probability system, pattern generator, or performance logic you think belongs in the project, write us an email and tell us about it.
laya.joinBody2: We are specifically interested in deterministic, algorithmic, stochastic, and rule-based generative systems that can run efficiently as part of the instrument.
laya.joinBody3: We do not accept generative-AI, inference-based, neural-network, cloud-compute, or GPU-dependent workflows.
laya.joinBody4: If your idea can be expressed as musical rules, mathematics, state machines, probability, pattern transformation, or other lightweight algorithmic logic, we’d be happy to hear from you.

meta.title: About  -  MontroneDSP
meta.description: MontroneDSP is an independent audio-software studio building distinctive instruments for producers, sound designers, and musicians.

about.title: About
about.lead: MontroneDSP is an independent audio-software studio focused on building distinctive instruments for producers, sound designers, and musicians who want more than familiar recreations.
about.p1: What began as a personal effort to turn original synthesis ideas into usable tools has grown into a wider family of instruments shaped by years of electronic-music production, experimentation, and technical research.
about.p2: Our work sits between precision and unpredictability: physical modelling, digital percussion, FM synthesis, modulation systems, and unusual signal-processing techniques brought together in instruments that remain direct, playable, and musical.
about.p3: We build for independent artists, adventurous producers, and professional studios alike.
about.p4: MontroneDSP is intentionally small and independent. That allows us to move quickly and listen closely to users.
about.mission: Make forward-looking sound design accessible without making it ordinary.
about.quote: For producers who have enough “warm analog character” already.
about.designP1: MontroneDSP is an independent Italian audio software studio shaped by a tradition in which engineering and design have rarely been treated as separate disciplines.
about.designP2: Our visual language draws from the clarity of Olivetti industrial design, the functional precision of Italian engineering, and the automotive work of studios such as Pininfarina and Bertone. These references are not used as decoration, but as a design principle: an object should communicate how it works through proportion, balance, materials, typography, and restraint. We approach a plugin interface much like an industrial designer approaches an instrument panel. Every control, meter, division, and line should have a reason to exist. Function comes first; character emerges naturally from the way those functions are organized.
about.frutigerAlt: Univers type family: weight and italic variations of the letter u
about.designP3: We are equally influenced by the discipline of Italian type design, particularly the work of Aldo Novarese, whose ability to combine strong identity with technical clarity remains an important reference.
about.designP4: Typography is treated as part of the instrument itself. Our interfaces often borrow from the proportions and highly legible glyph construction associated with Adrian Frutiger's work: open forms, clear differentiation between characters, economical spacing, and shapes designed to remain readable at a glance. These principles are especially relevant in audio software, where labels, values, meters, and controls must communicate immediately without competing with the task of listening.
about.designP5: The same philosophy extends to the software underneath. DSP architecture, interaction design, visual identity, and sound are developed as parts of the same instrument rather than as separate layers.

meta.title: DAWLESS | MontroneDSP
meta.description: DAWLESS is an experimental MontroneDSP project for early customers  -  a focused native environment for instruments and DSP, without a traditional DAW.
meta.ogDescription: A focused native environment for MontroneDSP instruments and DSP. Experimental project for early customers.
meta.ogImageAlt: MontroneDSP DAWLESS experimental music production environment

dawless.lead: A focused native environment for MontroneDSP instruments and DSP.
dawless.conceptP1: DAWLESS is an experimental MontroneDSP project created for our first customers. It gives direct access to our handwritten DSP engines and instruments inside a native environment  -  without needing to open a traditional DAW.
dawless.conceptP2: The aim is a simplified, optimized creative workstation: fewer distractions, fewer infinite choices, and a more defined workflow for music production and recording.
dawless.conceptP3: DAWLESS is not meant to replace every DAW. It is a focused creative environment where you can start, compose, sequence, record, and shape ideas with less friction  -  then move the work forward when the time is right.
dawless.workflowIntro: Most production environments offer everything at once. DAWLESS takes the opposite approach: a defined path through the work, with the tools that matter already in place.
dawless.workflowLi4: A clear workflow for creating, sequencing, recording, and shaping sound
dawless.workflowOutro: The goal is to combine the immediacy and focus of a hardware-like DAWless workflow with the sound quality and depth of MontroneDSP native instruments and DSP  -  and the convenience of exporting your work into a traditional professional production pipeline when you are ready.
dawless.nativeP1: DAWLESS is built around our own instruments and DSP  -  written specifically for the MontroneDSP ecosystem, not adapted from a generic host.
dawless.nativeP2: The sound engines are handwritten: processors and instruments developed in-house for this environment, without relying on a third-party host or off-the-shelf framework.
dawless.nativeP3: The environment is the engine. Sound design, synthesis, processing, and sequencing run on the same native foundation that powers our plugins  -  integrated from the start, not loaded in afterward.
dawless.exportP1: You will not be locked inside DAWLESS. When a project needs to continue in a traditional DAW  -  or be handed to a mixing or mastering engineer  -  the environment will include session exporters targeting the most widely used DAWs.
dawless.exportP2: The transition from a focused DAWLESS session into a full professional mix and master workflow is meant to be direct and painless. Start here. Finish wherever your process requires.

meta.title: Privacy  -  MontroneDSP

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead: MontroneDSP plugins are built to minimize data collection. Internet access is required only for license activation, license-related checks, purchases, downloads, support, and website operation  -  not to collect information about your music, sessions, presets, MIDI, or audio.
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how MontroneDSP processes personal data when you use our website, purchase or download our products, activate a license, or contact us for support.
privacy.h1p3: For privacy questions, correction requests, deletion requests, or any other data-related request, contact us at the email address above.
privacy.h2highlight: Martello, MartelloX2, Aura Shimmer, Swara XT, Membrana, and Laya are local instruments that run inside your DAW. We do not use subscriptions, always-online business models, or cloud-tied project storage.
privacy.h2p1: Your DAW sessions, presets, MIDI, and audio remain on your machine.
privacy.h2p2: MontroneDSP plugins do not collect usage analytics, telemetry, crash reports, diagnostic uploads, or information about how you make music.
privacy.h3p1: An internet connection may be required for license activation and occasional license-related checks. After activation, the plugin can be used offline within the terms of your license.
privacy.h3p2: To activate and manage a license, the licensing system may process information required to validate your purchase and manage your activations. This may include:
privacy.h3li8: basic technical information required for license validation
privacy.h3p3: This information is used only to activate the software, prevent license abuse, provide support, manage the number of allowed machines under your license, and protect the security of the licensing system.
privacy.h3basis: Lawful basis: performance of a contract, legitimate interests, and, where applicable, compliance with legal obligations.
privacy.h4p1: When you buy MontroneDSP products through the MontroneDSP store, payment and delivery may be handled by Gumroad or another payment/delivery provider.
privacy.h4p2: Gumroad processes the information required to complete your order, deliver your product, issue receipts, and handle payment-related services. MontroneDSP does not directly receive or store your payment card details.
privacy.h4p3: MontroneDSP may receive limited order information needed to deliver the product, provide support, manage licenses, and keep business records. This may include:
privacy.h4li6: country or tax-related information, where provided by the store platform
privacy.h4p4: Please refer to Gumroad's Privacy Policy for details about how Gumroad handles purchase and payment data.
privacy.h4basis: Lawful basis: performance of a contract, compliance with legal obligations, and legitimate interests.
privacy.h5p1: MontroneDSP offers a 7-day money-back guarantee on store purchases. If you request a refund within that period, we may process limited information related to your order, such as:
privacy.h5li3: order date and refund request details
privacy.h5p2: This information is used to verify eligibility, process refunds through the store platform, provide support, and keep necessary business records.
privacy.h5basis: Lawful basis: performance of a contract or pre-contractual request, and legitimate interests.
privacy.h6p1: If you email MontroneDSP for support, we receive your email address, your message, and any information you choose to include.
privacy.h6p2: This correspondence is used only to respond to your request, provide customer support, resolve technical issues, maintain necessary business records, and improve the reliability of our products.
privacy.h6p3: Please avoid sending unnecessary personal information, private project files, or sensitive data unless needed for support.
privacy.h6basis: Lawful basis: performance of a contract, legitimate interests, and, where applicable, compliance with legal obligations.
privacy.h7p1: MontroneDSP does not intentionally use analytics trackers or advertising trackers on the main website.
privacy.h7p3: Standard web server logs from the hosting provider may still record technical information such as:
privacy.h7li10: basic device or technical request data
privacy.h7p4: These logs are used for security, maintenance, troubleshooting, abuse prevention, and normal website operation.
privacy.h7p5: Third-party services linked from the website, such as Gumroad or other payment/download providers, may use their own cookies, logs, and privacy practices.
privacy.h7basis: Lawful basis: legitimate interests and, where applicable, consent or compliance with legal obligations.
privacy.h8p1: MontroneDSP may use trusted service providers to operate the website, sell products, deliver downloads, activate licenses, manage email, and provide support.
privacy.h8p2: Depending on the product and purchase flow, these may include:
privacy.h8li1: Gumroad, for store purchases, payments, delivery, receipts, and related services
privacy.h8li2: licensing/activation providers, such as Keygen or equivalent licensing infrastructure
privacy.h8li5: technical service providers needed for security, maintenance, and support
privacy.h8p3: These providers process data only as needed to provide their services, according to their own privacy policies and applicable data protection requirements.
privacy.h8p4: We do not sell your personal data.
privacy.h9p1: Some service providers may be based outside the European Economic Area or may process data in countries outside the European Economic Area.
privacy.h9p2: Where required, transfers are handled using appropriate safeguards, such as contractual protections, adequacy decisions, or other mechanisms permitted by applicable data protection law.
privacy.h10p1: We keep personal data only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purposes described in this Privacy Policy.
privacy.h10li1: support emails are kept as long as needed for customer service, technical support, and reasonable business record-keeping
privacy.h10li2: license and activation records are kept as long as needed to provide access to the software, manage activations, prevent fraud or abuse, and support customers
privacy.h10li3: purchase records are kept as required for accounting, tax, fraud prevention, customer support, and legal obligations
privacy.h10li4: demo download records are kept as long as needed for website operation, support, product improvement, and reasonable business records
privacy.h10li5: website server logs are retained according to the hosting provider's normal security and maintenance policies
privacy.h10p3: When personal data is no longer needed, it will be deleted, anonymized, or retained only where required by law or legitimate business needs.
privacy.h11p1: Depending on your location and applicable law, you may have the right to:
privacy.h11li5: object to processing based on legitimate interests
privacy.h11li7: withdraw consent where processing is based on consent
privacy.h11li8: lodge a complaint with a data protection authority
privacy.h11p3: We may need to verify your identity before responding to certain requests.
privacy.h12p1: If you believe your personal data has been processed in a way that violates applicable data protection law, you have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
privacy.h12p2: In Italy, the competent authority is:
privacy.h12p3: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
privacy.h12p4: You may also contact the data protection authority in your country of residence, workplace, or the place where the alleged violation occurred.
privacy.h13p1: MontroneDSP does not use your personal data for automated profiling, behavioral advertising, or automated decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects.
privacy.h13p2: License activation may automatically check whether a license is valid and whether the allowed number of activations has been reached. This is used only for software licensing and anti-abuse purposes.
privacy.h14p1: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time, for example if we change our store, licensing system, website, support process, or legal requirements.
privacy.h14p2: The latest version will be published on the MontroneDSP website with the updated date.

modi.lead: Archived legacy concept for a tuned resonator instrument.
modi.cta: Visit the current free tools page
modi.title: This page preserves the earlier Modi-focused version of the free experience.
modi.body1: The current free page is now focused on practical tools and a simpler layout. This archived page remains available as a reference for the earlier resonator-instrument concept.
modi.body2: It explored struck physical tones, tuned resonant bodies, mallet percussion, and a compact synthesis approach around contact, damping, and bloom.
